detailed_description: The Cron Expression Generator helps you assemble a standard five-field cron expression in the browser. Choose one of the quick presets or edit the minute, hour, day of month, month, and weekday fields directly, then review the generated expression and a simple human-readable summary. A small reference explains common cron characters such as asterisks, commas, ranges, and step values, and the final expression can be copied to your clipboard for use in schedulers that accept five-field cron syntax.
usage_steps: Start from a quick preset such as every minute, every hour, every weekday, or every 5 minutes
Edit the minute, hour, day, month, and weekday text fields when you need a custom cron expression
Review the generated five-field expression and the simple readable description below it
Use the special-character reference for wildcards, lists, ranges, and step values
Click Copy to copy the cron expression to your clipboard
usage_examples: A system administrator creates a nightly database backup cron job that runs at 02:30 AM on weekdays: '30 2 * * 1-5'
A developer schedules a CI/CD pipeline to trigger every 15 minutes during work hours: '*/15 9-17 * * 1-5'
An IT engineer prepares a first-day-of-month maintenance schedule: '0 0 1 * *'
A data analyst prepares a quarterly ETL schedule by entering the month field manually: '15 1 * 1,4,7,10 *'
